summary: Tadji Airport is a small airstrip serving the coastal town of Aitape in Papua New Guinea's Sandaun Province (formerly West Sepik). The airfield has notable World War II history, having served as an Allied base during the New Guinea campaign following the landing at Aitape in 1944. Today it functions primarily as a regional airport supporting local communities, missionaries, and aid operations in this remote part of the Sepik coast.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Tadji Airport?
A: The airport serves the town of Aitape and surrounding villages, providing essential transport links for residents, missionaries, and humanitarian missions in this remote coastal region of Papua New Guinea.

Q: Does Tadji Airport have scheduled commercial service?
A: Yes, the airport receives regular scheduled flights operated by PNG Air, connecting Aitape to other towns in the region including Wewak.

Q: What is the airport's historical significance?
A: Tadji was an important World War II airstrip used by Allied forces during the New Guinea campaign, supporting operations along the northern coast in 1944-1945.

Q: What is the runway like at Tadji Airport?
A: The airport has a single short unpaved or lightly surfaced runway, typical of rural Papua New Guinea airfields, and can only accommodate small turboprop aircraft.
transport_tips: There are no public buses or taxis serving the airport; travelers should arrange pickup in advance with their hotel, a local contact, or the airline. The town of Aitape is only a short drive away, so most accommodations and the town center are within 10-15 minutes by vehicle. Missionary aircraft and charter planes are also common at Tadji, so be prepared to share the apron with small Cessna-type aircraft.
local_tip: Flights are frequently delayed or rescheduled due to weather and limited aircraft availability in PNG's Sandaun Province, so build at least a full extra day of buffer into your travel plans when connecting through Aitape.
